items.title: "Kid Thomas" Valentine Interview, 1964-03-21
items.q: I went on through playing with different fellows with the alto. Played with old man Jackson, the bass player. ... Is that Eddie Jackson? Eddie Jackson, yes. String bass at that band, or... Oh, he was playing the sousaphone. ... And we played different places.

ctx.x: Well, I played that for a while. Then later on, that, uh, fellas began falling out. Nice we had supposed to have had instructions. Fellas began having dates, you know. Couldn't come out to rehearsal, uh, instructions. So, therefore, that, uh, caused the band to disband, see. And, uh, from that, well, the fellas went astray. And, uh, I wonder if you can hear me. Yeah. Mm-hmm. So, therefore, that's, uh, that's where I started music, and from the church, on the violin. What instrument did you take? And you must have…
All right, we're rolling. What's your name?

items.title: "Kid Thomas" Valentine Interview, 1959-11-08
items.q: And all, and Eddie Jackson, you see, when Eddie Jackson was playing in the brass band, you could hear him for miles

ctx.x: And the people used to follow the band from the startin' to the finish. That's right. From the startin' to the finish. You go all the way to the graveyard, okay, you go up to Gretna, they go, go to Gretna, and back, you see? And all, and Eddie Jackson, you see, when Eddie Jackson was playing in the brass band, you could hear him for miles, you see? That's right, yeah. And them youngsters really know why they had to say, oh, they, they, somebody had blocks from here. They know, because they used to hear him. They…
He came from over the river too, didn't he?
